name: GA-10
label: Likely R

key_factors: Houston Gaines' large fundraising and outside-spending advantage over Pam Delancy
Prediction markets price Republican win at ~95%
Open seat after Mike Collins retired to run for Senate
model.rationale: The district's R+11 lean and a Republican fundraising and outside-spending edge for Houston Gaines point to a comfortable Republican hold, and markets price a Republican win around 95%. The open seat adds some uncertainty, but no evidence suggests a competitive race.
model.watch: A surge of Democratic spending or polling showing Gaines underperforming in the Athens-area portion of the district would be the main signal of a closer race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Mike Collins (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Republicans are strongly favored to hold this open northeast Georgia seat, which backed Trump by a wide margin and has a Republican-favoring partisan lean. Incumbent Mike Collins left the seat to run for Senate, and state Rep. Houston Gaines enters the general election with a major financial advantage, having raised about $2.3 million with roughly $1.5 million in outside support. Democrat Pam Delancy has raised only about $23,000 and has no outside backing.

Prediction markets give Republicans about a 95% chance of winning, and no expert raters or public polls flag the race as competitive. The forecast expects a Republican win by roughly fourteen points, with the open-seat dynamic and thin polling leaving modest room for error.
